findings.explanation: getUri performs three ordered synchronous handoffs: mergeConfig(this.defaults, config) produces the configuration used from then on; buildFullPath receives exactly mergedConfig.baseURL, mergedConfig.url, and mergedConfig.allowAbsoluteUrls; buildURL then receives exactly that full-path string, mergedConfig.params, and mergedConfig.paramsSerializer. Under the stated inputs it returns the resulting URI string directly, not a response or request promise. There is no catch boundary, so errors from merging, path construction, a serializer, conversion, or encoding escape synchronously. The method does not call request(), construct an interceptor chain, invoke an adapter, or dispatch network traffic; it only computes the URI.

mergeConfig creates a new top-level result and does not assign into either ordinary input configuration. The url entry uses valueFromConfig2, so only a defined per-call url is selected: an instance-default url is not inherited. baseURL and paramsSerializer use defaultToConfig2: a per-call undefined behaves as not supplied and falls back to the instance default, while null is a supplied override. Thus null paramsSerializer disables an inherited serializer, and null or an empty-string baseURL suppresses an inherited base. A defined per-call paramsSerializer object replaces, rather than merges with, the default serializer object. params and allowAbsoluteUrls are absent from mergeMap and therefore use mergeDeepProperties: a top-level undefined falls back to the default, while a non-undefined per-call value wins (including null for params and either boolean for allowAbsoluteUrls). When both selected values are plain objects, utility merge recursively combines them with later/per-call properties taking precedence; a nested per-call undefined also takes precedence and is subsequently omitted during default parameter traversal. Arrays are replaced with a shallow slice of the selected later array, not concatenated. Plain-object containers are recreated recursively, but arbitrary non-plain values are returned by reference. Consequently a native URLSearchParams used as params—and non-plain leaves such as Dates inside otherwise copied params—does not receive a universal deep clone.

isAbsoluteURL recognizes only strings beginning with either // or a case-insensitive scheme of the form letter followed by letters, digits, plus, period, or hyphen and then ://. Protocol-relative URLs therefore count as absolute; ordinary paths and schemes without // do not. With a truthy, nonempty baseURL, a relative requested URL is always combined. An absolute or protocol-relative requested URL is combined only when allowAbsoluteUrls is explicitly false; when that option is true or absent, the requested absolute URL is returned unchanged. If baseURL is absent, null, or empty, its falsiness prevents combination even when allowAbsoluteUrls is false. combineURLs is literal string joining: for a nonempty requested part it removes the final one-or-two-slash match from the base, inserts '/', and removes all leading slashes from the requested part; if the requested part is empty it returns the base unchanged. It is not URL resolution: it does not enforce origins, interpret dot segments, normalize traversal, or otherwise validate the resulting path.

buildURL first returns url unchanged when params is falsy, covering absent, undefined, and null params; no serializer runs and an existing fragment remains. A function-form paramsSerializer is normalized to {serialize: originalFunction}; it is then called as serialize(params, normalizedOptions). For object form, options.serialize is called as serialize(params, options). A custom serializer takes precedence even when params is a native URLSearchParams and its returned string is used verbatim. Without one, native URLSearchParams uses its own toString(); all other in-scope params take the AxiosURLSearchParams path. options.encode is selected as the custom encoder only for that default AxiosURLSearchParams pair-to-string path, where it is invoked for each key and value and receives the value plus AxiosURLSearchParams' internal encoder as its second argument. It is bypassed by both custom serialization and native URLSearchParams.toString(). Serializer and encoder exceptions are not caught and propagate synchronously through getUri. Fragment removal and separator insertion happen only for a truthy serialized string: everything from the first # onward is removed, then '?' is appended if the remaining URL has no question mark, otherwise '&' is appended. An empty serializer result—or an empty default/native serialization—leaves the entire original URL, including any fragment, unchanged.

In the default plain-object branch, buildURL constructs AxiosURLSearchParams, which initializes a pair array and passes itself to toFormData. The traversal calls its append method to accumulate [key, value] pairs; toString later encodes each side, emits key=value, and joins pairs with '&'. The recursive build skips null and undefined object members before invoking the visitor. A top-level flat-array property is expanded under the default indexes:false mode into repeated key[] pairs, with null, undefined, and holes omitted. The special flat-array expansion is guarded by !path; a flat array nested below an object instead follows recursive traversal and receives bracketed numeric path components, such as a[b][0]. Nested plain objects likewise recurse, and default dots:false rendering produces names such as a[b]. Dates become toISOString() strings and booleans become 'true' or 'false'; ordinary scalar values proceed to encoding. The URI builder's default encoder applies encodeURIComponent, changes spaces from %20 to '+', restores colon, dollar, and comma as literal ':', '$', and ',', and leaves brackets percent-encoded as %5B and %5D. These visitor, conversion, key-shape, and encoder rules belong only to the default plain-object path. Native URLSearchParams bypasses them and supplies its own toString(), while a custom serializer bypasses materialization and contributes its returned string verbatim.
